sentence: Waterings whose fields are null or malformed render as-is on /waterings and the dashboard (e.g. 'Never', blank bed, 'x L', raw 'garbage' date) instead of placeholders.
evidence: Reproduced in the browser: signed in as the demo user, mocked GET /api/waterings with page.route to return [{id:1,bed_id:1,bed_name:null,watered_on:null,watered_at:'garbage',litres:'x'},{id:2,...all null}], then went to /waterings and the dashboard by client-side navigation (on a full page load the server renders the page and the mock is skipped). /waterings rows: 'garbage\t\tx L\tDelete watering of' and 'Never\t\t–\tDelete watering of'; the dashboard showed the same. So the rendering the reports describe does happen. But the real backend cannot send this data. WateringOut (backend/schemas.py:146) declares bed_name: str, watered_on: date (required) and litres: float | None, and FastAPI validates responses against it. The list query uses an inner JOIN on beds (routers/waterings.py:18-20), and waterings.bed_id is NOT NULL with ON DELETE RESTRICT (db.py:38), so bed_name and watered_on are always present and litres is a number or null. Null litres already shows '–'. A bad date showing raw text matches how the existing formatDate/formatDateTime helpers treat bad values elsewhere in the app. The request does not ask the client to guard against payloads that break the API contract. The output only appears with a hand-made response that the server would reject, so it is not a defect a user could hit.
